items.briefing:
Cybercriminals are now sending malicious calendar invites to trick people into clicking phishing links — if you receive an unexpected meeting invitation, especially from an unknown sender, be cautious before accepting or clicking any links inside it. This tactic is increasingly being used to bypass email security filters, making it harder for standard tools to catch.

Separately, a Canadian man has pleaded guilty over extortion attacks linked to the Snowflake data breach, a reminder that cloud data theft carries serious real-world consequences for organisations storing sensitive information online.

**Practical tip:** Treat unexpected calendar invites the same way you would suspicious emails — don't click embedded links without verifying the sender first.
